brief.title: The Glass Tide
brief.premise: A junior tide-warden discovers that the lagoon gates are silting shut weeks ahead of schedule, and must convince the guilds to halt the glassblowing season before the city loses the tide that powers it.
constraints: No combustion engines or fossil fuels anywhere in the setting.

world.name: The Tidal Conservatories
world.description: A terraced city grown into a shallow lagoon, where mangrove walls, vitrified glass locks and tide-mills turn the twice-daily flood into power, food and light.

locations.name: The Glassgate Locks
locations.description: Vitrified gates that meter the tide into the lagoon; their sills are silting up weeks ahead of the survey.

locations.name: The Mangrove Terraces
locations.description: Stepped root-gardens where families tend silt-traps and grow the city's rice and reed stock.

locations.name: The Algae Fields
locations.description: Raft-farms of oil algae that feed the kiln digesters and the lamp vats.

locations.name: Bellmaker's Quay
locations.description: The wharf where channel bells and glass floats are cast, and the seat of the glassblower guilds.

factions.name: The Tide Wardens
factions.description: Engineers sworn to keep the locks clear and read the tide tables for the whole lagoon.

factions.name: The Glassblower Guild
factions.description: Artisans who fire their kilns on lagoon gas and hold the charter for every bell and window.

factions.name: The Ferry Cooperative
factions.description: Sail and paddle barge crews who haul harvest, glass and dredged silt across the lagoon.

rules.statement: All power in the city comes from the tide, the sun or the algae digesters; combustion engines are banned by charter.
Every gate crew must clear its lock before each spring tide, whatever the guild calendar says.
A channel bell cast out of tune must be recast within a day, because the whole lagoon navigates by its ring.
Whoever dredges silt from the locks owns the fertile silt, but must spread it on the terraces within a season.

history.name: The Raising of the Glassgates
history.description: The first locks were fused from lagoon glass so the tide could be let in without drowning the terraces.

history.name: The Great Silting
history.description: A storm choked the gates with silt; the city went hungry until the terraces dug the locks out.

history.name: The Bell Charter
history.description: After a night collision in fog, the guilds bound themselves to recast any mistuned channel bell within a day.

conflicts.name: The Kiln Calendar
conflicts.description: The Glassblower Guild wants a long firing season, but the Tide Wardens need the gates shut for dredging before the spring tide.

conflicts.name: The Silt Rights
conflicts.description: The Ferry Cooperative claims the rich silt it dredges, while the Tide Wardens say it belongs to the terrace commons.

characters.name: Mara Ilek
characters.description: A junior tide-warden who keeps the sounding poles at the Glassgate Locks and still writes her survey notes in her mother's hand.
characters.motivation: To prove the locks are silting early, before the city loses the tide it runs on.
characters.goal: Get the gates dredged before the spring tide arrives.
characters.flaw: She assumes the soundings will persuade people by themselves.
characters.internal_conflict: She fears becoming the alarmist the guilds once called her mother.
characters.external_conflict: The guild masters refuse to shorten the firing season for a junior warden's numbers.

abilities.name: Silt-reading
abilities.description: Reads the settle lines on a sounding pole to judge how fast a channel is filling.

characters.arc: Mara learns to carry her proof into the guild halls and let others help her hold the gate.

characters.name: Oren Pell
characters.description: Master of the Glassblower Guild, whose kilns keep half the quay employed and whose word sets the firing calendar.
characters.motivation: To protect the firing season his guild's families depend on.
characters.goal: Keep the locks open through the full firing season.
characters.flaw: He cannot admit a trade-off once he has made it.
characters.internal_conflict: He has read the same tide tables as Mara and knows what they say.
characters.external_conflict: Mara's soundings prove the silting is early, and the wardens want the gates closed.

abilities.name: Furnace-sense
abilities.description: Judges a kiln's heat and temper by the sound of its draw.

characters.arc: Pell must choose between the guild's season and the lagoon that feeds it.

characters.name: Sana Duro
characters.description: A cooperative barge pilot who hauls algae and dredged silt between the fields and the terraces.
characters.motivation: To keep the Ferry Cooperative solvent and fairly paid.
characters.goal: Win the dredging contract without selling the cooperative's silt rights.
characters.flaw: She bargains when she should listen.
characters.internal_conflict: She wants the wardens' contract but distrusts their charter.
characters.external_conflict: Both the wardens and the guild want her barge and her silence.

abilities.name: Channel-reading
abilities.description: Feels a channel's depth through the barge's tiller in fog or darkness.

characters.arc: Sana stakes her barge on the wardens' evidence and drags the truth into the open.

relationships.description: Mara hires Sana's barge to sound the gate channels.
relationships.conflict: Sana's price is a say in who owns the dredged silt.

relationships.description: Pell dismissed Mara's soundings as apprentice work.
relationships.conflict: His guild cannot afford the closure she demands.

storyboard.title: The Glass Tide
storyboard.logline: A junior tide-warden proves the lagoon gates are silting early and forces the guilds to choose between the firing season and the tide.
storyboard.theme: commons and the cost of proof

scenes.title: The Soundings
scenes.summary: Mara reads the settle lines at the Glassgate Locks and finds the sills silting weeks ahead of the survey.
scenes.conflict: The numbers contradict the guild calendar.
scenes.outcome: Mara certifies the early silting in the wardens' log.

scenes.title: The Guild's Answer
scenes.summary: Mara takes the soundings to Bellmaker's Quay, where Oren Pell dismisses them as apprentice work and refuses to shorten the firing season.
scenes.conflict: Pell will not trade the guild's season for a junior warden's numbers.
scenes.outcome: The petition is refused; Mara must find another lever.

scenes.title: The Barge Charter
scenes.summary: Mara charters Sana's barge at the Algae Fields to run a full channel sounding the guild cannot dispute.
scenes.conflict: Sana demands a voice in the silt rights for her help.
scenes.outcome: Sana signs on; the sounding begins at the next ebb.

scenes.title: Two Fingers of Water
scenes.summary: The channel survey proves the locks will shoal shut before the firing season ends, days ahead of the spring tide.
scenes.conflict: The proof means the season must end early.
scenes.outcome: The survey is witnessed and logged beyond dispute.

scenes.title: The Muster Bell
scenes.summary: Mara rings the muster bell at the Quay to force a guild vote; as the masters argue, the ebb itself strands a kiln barge, and Pell concedes.
scenes.conflict: Pell stakes his mastership on the season holding.
scenes.outcome: The guild votes to dredge; the season is shortened, not lost.

scenes.title: Silt on the Terraces
scenes.summary: Guild crews and the cooperative dredge the locks together, and the rich silt is spread on the Mangrove Terraces under a shared charter.
scenes.goal: Clear the locks before the spring tide.
scenes.conflict: The silt rights must be shared without a new quarrel.
scenes.outcome: The gates clear in time; the silt feeds the terraces and the charter is amended.

evidence_summary: The world, cast and storyboard satisfy the brief's tide-powered solarpunk setting; deterministic validators are clean and there are no blocking defects.
